answer: Split grading into disjoint shards: three panels with no shared members score each answer, and a grade counts only when two panels agree. A sybil attacker must win majorities inside whole panels, not slip a few accounts into one pool. One fake identity buys one seat in one panel, so a thousand fakes scattered across panels win nothing, while a thousand crammed into one panel trip the size cap and expose the cluster. Two survey teams must agree before a summit route is marked; the panels anchor trust the same way, and no single forge of fake graders can stamp both approvals.
